(A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.citation_text: 750.140 - A) Pot roast portioned in plastic baggies and stored in a large plastic container in the walkin cooler had internal temperatures of 84F-96F. Date on label was 10/24, but no time was indicated. Owner verified the pot roast was pulled from oven at ~1:30-2p. Temperature was checked around 2:30p. Owner was allowed to keep pot roast, and portions were placed on a backing sheet in the walkin freezer to help rapidly drop the temperature.  B) Four pans of cheese sauce with prep date 10/24 stacked together in walkin cooler had surface temperatures at 40F-45F. Internal temperatures for cheese sauce in the middle two containers were at 49F and 54F. Cheese sauce in bottom container had internal temperature of 47, and cheese sauce in top container had internal temperature of 41F-42F. Cheese sauce above 42F was discarded in the trash by owner. Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F within 2 hours and from 70F to 41F/below within additional 4 hours. Total cooling time must not exceed 6 hours. Allow heat to vent off of cooling foods and do not store hot products stacked together in pans or in baggies when foods are still hot. Utilize ice baths, the walkin freezer, and ice wands to help rapidly cool cooked foods.

Cooked potentially hazardous foods (PHF) shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F w/in 2hrs and from 70F to 41F/below w/in additional 4hrs. Total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs. findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.citation_text: 750.140 - Three pans of cooked ground beef made at 9:15am today were stacked together in the walkin cooler. Surface temperature was 105F (top pan). Pans were moved to the walkin freezer at 10am. At 10:25am the internal temperatures were 140F-150F. The containers were covered and had not been checked or separated out in to smaller batches or stirred. The product was not going to reach 70F within the 2 hour time frame. Cooked potentially hazardous foods must be cooled from 135F to 70F within 2 hours and from 70F to 41F/below within 4 hours. Separate foods in to shallow pans, place on ice baths, stir frequently, monitor temperatures, and leave containers uncovered until foods have properly cooled. The owner was informed of the issue and said she would take care of the product.
